messages:
deploy-bot: Starting rollout: release/2026-03-20. Canary 5% -> ramp plan [5m, +15m, +10m] to 100% over 30m. Feature flag `new-routing` -> enabled in canary. Model pin: v2.4.1.

alice-platform: Observability note: adding the canary now. Will monitor latency and error rate.

carol-sre: @alice-platform seeing a small latency blip on canary hosts, p50 up ~120ms -> 240ms, p95 up ~500ms since 40s after canary start. 5xx spike from 0.02% -> 0.6%.

ben-release: Noted. Are logs blaming model inference time or infra?

dinesh-eng: Looking at inference logs — a couple of GPUs hit CPU-side batching saturation. Sample stack: `kv-cache load` spikes.

carol-sre: Threshold breached: error-rate > 0.5% for 2 consecutive mins. Auto-policy: pause rollout. deploy-bot: Pausing rollout at 5% (policy: error-rate).

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by policy (error_rate). Canary traffic remains at 5%. Actions: `--resume`, `--rollback`, or `--pin`.

alice-platform: Suggest we hold canary, do quick revert of feature flag for prod (disable `new-routing` in prod) while we triage.

ben-release: Agreed. Quick plan: 1) disable ff in prod 2) pin routing to v2.4.0 3) record release note + incident flag. Who toggles?

release-manager: I'll flip the flag. Doing `ffctl toggle set new-routing false --env=prod --by=release-manager` now.

release-manager: `> success: new-routing set to false (prod) at 1717203498` :white_check_mark:

carol-sre: Observability: error-rate dropping back toward baseline; latency recovering. Holding for 3 mins to confirm.

dinesh-eng: While flag was off, I pinned the serving config back to model v2.4.0 on canary hosts: `redwoodctl pin model routing-service v2.4.0 --scope=canary --reason="rollback after latency spike"`

deploy-bot: Noted: model pin applied. Current canary model v2.4.0.

alice-platform: Good. dev/prod diff looks clean. Ben, can you draft a 1-paragraph release note about the rollback + follow-ups? Keep it in the release channel and changelog.

ben-release: Will do. Draft: "Aborted canary for release/2026-03-20 after increased latency and error-rate during a canary test for `new-routing`. Feature flag disabled in prod and routing model pinned to v2.4.0. Investigating batching-edge case; follow-up to include mitigation and longer canary with throttled traffic."

release-manager: Posting note to #release-notes and adding `incident:canary` tag.

sre-oncall: Adding follow-up runbook tasks: (1) collect full KV-cache timelines from canary hosts (2) reproduce with smaller batch sizes (3) run longer 1% canary tomorrow during low-traffic window.

deploy-bot: Rollout remains paused at 5% and feature flag is disabled in prod. If you want to resume a tuned canary, use `deploy-bot resume --manual` after approvals.

alice-platform: Thanks everyone. Marking this thread as post-deploy hold; we'll reconvene in the morning for a deeper investigation. :spiral_calendar_pad:

ben-release: pinging performance-ml to look at quantization/kv-cache interactions first thing.

carol-sre: Confirmed stable for 6 mins. Removing immediate alerting noise. Keeping close watch during next attempted rollouts.

release-manager: Closing immediate action items. Will link the changelog and incident ticket here shortly: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-2026-0342

sre-oncall: ETA for next canary attempt: 2026-03-21 03:00 UTC (low traffic). We'll schedule a gradual ramp with 1% -> 2% -> 5% over 45m and keep flag toggles manual.

alice-platform: Sounds good. End of thread.
